newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe says in talks on possible deal.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe says in talks on possible deal.

text.p: H&R Block Inc., which owns about 80 percent of online service CompuServe Corp., said Wednesday that the two companies are in discussions with a third party regarding a possible business combination involving CompuServe.
But they added that there are no assurances that the talks will result in any agreement or transaction.
On Tuesday, shares of CompuServe, the nation's second-largest online service, jumped on a rumour that industry leader America Online Inc. was in talks to buy its rival.
Block and Compuserve did not specify in the statement who was involved in the discussions. Company officials were not immediately available to comment on the statement.
AOL officials also could not be reached, but AOL earlier declined to comment on speculation it was interested in Compuserve.

Compuserve's stock, which trades separately from Block's, was up 25 cents at $11.25 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq before it was halted pending news, while AOL lost $1.50 to $45 on the New York Stock Exchange.
